shortDescription: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index rose on Thursday, helped by stronger rates in the capesize vessel category.

children: The Baltic Exchange's dry bulk freight index rose on Thursday, helped by stronger rates in the capesize vessel category.
, which tracks rates for capesize, panamax and supramax vessels, rose 9 points, or 0.3%, to 3,336 points.
The capesize index (.BACI) rose 44 points, or 0.8%, to 5,656 points.
Average daily earnings for capesize vessels (.BATCA), which typically transport 150,000-ton cargoes, including iron ore and coal, increased by $396 to $47,793.
Iron ore prices rose for a second session, as Chinese steelmakers stepped up seaborne purchases ahead of a national holiday, although shrinking steel margins clouded the demand outlook.
The panamax index (.BPNI) fell 43 points, or 1.8%, to 2,282 points.
Average daily earnings for panamax vessels (.BPWT), which usually carry 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, fell $392 to $20,535.
Among smaller vessels, the supramax index (.BSIS) was up 14 points, or 0.8%, at 1,762.
